source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0, via Overpass API

buildings.floor_area_ratio_withheld_because: building:levels is present on a minority of footprints, so a ratio computed from the tagged subset would describe that subset and be read as describing the site

limits: OpenStreetMap is crowd-sourced: absence of a street or a building is absence from the map, not from the ground.
Dual carriageways are mapped as two ways, which raises network length against a centreline-based figure; the density here is an upper estimate for that reason.
Blocks are the cells enclosed by mapped streets, not cadastral parcels, and no tenure information is used or implied.

Block shares are quoted against the land inside closed cells, not against the boundary: cells along the edge of the site are not closed by mapped streets, so the two denominators differ by more than a factor of two.

Whether a large cell is park, campus, water or heritage is decided from OSM tags on the polygons inside it, at a 50% majority. A cell that is mostly a walled compound carrying no landuse tag counts as built.
Junctions are shared OSM nodes, so grade-separated crossings are correctly not counted as junctions and the figure is lower than a plan-crossing count.
These are readings of the existing fabric. They are not proposed control values and nothing here may be read as a plot ratio, height limit or redline.
